title: 1995 AHSME Problem 24
statement: There exist positive integers \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C,\) with no common factor greater than \(1,\) such that \[A\log_{200}5+B\log_{200}2=C.\] What is \(A+B+C?\)

solutions.text: Combining logarithms gives \[ \log_{200}(5^A2^B)=C, \] so \(5^A2^B=200^C=5^{2C}2^{3C}.\) Hence \(A=2C\) and \(B=3C.\) The relatively prime positive triple is \((A,B,C)=(2,3,1),\) whose sum is \(6.\) Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Combine the left side into one logarithm
